_comment: Shared cross-back-end conformance fixture for provider-fragment composition (docs/spec/provider-fragment.md §Composition rules). The SAME scenarios are asserted against dispatcher/vercel/src/provider.rs and dispatcher/claude-code-cli/src/provider.rs, which parse the format independently because each composes into its own target's capability types. Only ENGINE-NEUTRAL rules live here — the merge and safety semantics both back-ends must agree on. Anything engine-specific (how a granted tool is spelled) is asserted in that back-end's own suite instead. A drift in the merge rules fails whichever side moved away from this file.

scenarios.name: a fragment adds a capability the base lacks
a fragment may not redefine a safety-critical base capability
scenarios.error_contains: already provided by the base target

scenarios.name: a fragment whose engine does not match the target is rejected
two fragments claiming one capability collide, even sharing a provider string
scenarios.error_contains: at most one provider source per capability

scenarios.name: a tool binding with no profile entry anywhere is refused
scenarios._note: Uses a bare-label source deliberately: an mcp: source would trip the via/source coherence check first (in both back-ends), and this scenario is about the missing profile entry.

scenarios.name: a malformed mcp source is refused
via must name the same server the tool source comes from
scenarios.error_contains: so the report and the tool
